To secure a multi-agent economy against Sybil attacks without relying on centralized KYC, networks can implement a cryptographic reputation
 staking model resembling a crystal lattice, where nodes lock native tokens to validate transitions. An attacker seeking to flood the network must commit substantial capital to forge authenticated channels, turning every consensus whisper into a costly financial commitment. This economic ridge ensures that the cost of generating fake identities scales exponentially faster than the potential rewards of manipulating the shared ledger.
